title: 真假金丝雀的博弈第3章
content_zh:
第3章 挥杆与过招

    周六下午两点，顾西辞的车准时出现在公寓楼下。

    我拉开后排车门的时候，他正低头看手机，头也不抬地说了句：“坐前面。”

    “后排宽敞。”

    “坐前面。我不是你的司机。”

    我关上后排车门，坐进副驾驶。他的车里有一股淡淡的雪松味，是车载香薰的味道，和他办公室里的味道一样。中控台上放着一杯美式咖啡，已经喝了一半，旁边是一杯没拆封的拿铁。

    “给我的？”

    “提神。你今天要站四个小时。”

    我拆开拿铁的盖子喝了一口。温的，不是烫的。顾西辞记得我不喝烫的咖啡——以前每次他给我带咖啡，都会让店员做成温的。这个习惯保持了多久？八年还是九年？他居然还没忘。

    “球场在青城那边，开车一个半小时。趁这个时间跟你说说规则。”他发动车子，单手打方向盘，“今天不是正式比赛，是我私下的练习局。但到场的人里有一部分会是下周邀请赛的参赛者，你得提前熟悉他们的路数。”

    “哪些人？”

    “林子明你见过了，林氏地产的。今天还有三个人——万盛集团的执行副总裁许向平，做私募的陈鹤东，还有青城高尔夫俱乐部的老板赵启年。赵启年不重要，许向平和陈鹤东是你今天要重点观察的对象。”

    “许向平。万盛集团。是不是之前跟你有过摩擦的那个？”

    他侧头看了我一眼：“你怎么知道？”

    “查的。你助理备忘录里写过一行——许向平在去年的并购案里跟顾氏竞价到最后一天，最后输了。旁边备注了四个字，来者不善。”

    顾西辞沉默了几秒，然后轻轻笑了一声：“你把我助理的备忘录当成情报站了？”

    “你的助理是你的助理，不是我的。我得靠自己做背调。”

    “好，那你知不知道陈鹤东是谁？”

    “知春资本的创始人，专投消费赛道。去年他投了一个新茶饮品牌，半年翻了四倍。圈子里叫他点金手，但脾气特别差，曾经因为对赌协议把一个创业者逼到卖房还债。”

    顾西辞挑起一边眉毛：“你查了多久？”

    “昨晚查了两个小时。你们这些人的公开资料太多了，发布会、采访、财经报道，随便翻翻就能拼出一张关系网。”

    “那你说说看，这三个人之间什么关系？”

    “许向平和陈鹤东是大学同学，都是清华经管毕业的。赵启年是许向平的姐夫，所以青城俱乐部等于是许向平的地盘。你今天带我去这个地方打球，等于是在许向平的主场里插了一面顾氏的旗。”

    顾西辞的手指在方向盘上轻轻敲了两下。这是他思考时的习惯，用食指敲击手边最近的东西，节奏不快不慢，每次三下。

    “你漏了一点。”他说。

    “哪一点？”

    “许向平的太太也姓林。林氏地产的林。”

    “所以他是林子明的女婿？”

    “没错。”

    我把这几个人的关系在脑子里重新画了一遍。林子明的女婿是许向平，许向平的大学同学是陈鹤东，许向平的姐夫是球场的老板。这群人是一家子加上一个老同学，铁板一块。顾西辞在这个局里，等于是单枪匹马闯进了别人家的后院。

    “你今天带我来，是想让我做什么？”

    “当我的搭档。”他的语气很平淡，好像在说今天天气不错，“高尔夫球场上最考验默契的不是对手之间的较量，是搭档之间的配合。我挥杆的时候，你要知道站在哪里。我跟人谈事的时候，你要知道什么时候开口、什么时候闭嘴。昨天林氏晚宴你做得不错，但那种场合好应付——端着酒杯笑就行。今天不一样。”

    “哪里不一样？”

    “今天不只是社交，是比赛。赛场上的人看不起花瓶。”

    他把“花瓶”两个字说得很轻，但很清楚。我没有接话。

    青城高尔夫俱乐部建在半山腰上，从停车场往会所走的路上能看到整个球场的全景。草坪修剪得整整齐齐，果岭像一块块绿色的绒毯铺在山坡上，沙坑的白沙在阳光下亮得晃眼。空气里有草屑的清香和淡淡的汽油味，是草坪维护车的味道。

    会所是中式风格的建筑，青砖灰瓦，门口立着两棵银杏树。服务生穿着统一的白衬衫和米色马甲，看见顾西辞就迎上来，脸上带着训练有素的微笑。

    “顾总，赵总已经在球场等您了。许总和陈总也到了，在茶室休息。”

    “先不去茶室。给我开一个练习场。”

    “好的，您这边请。”

    练习场在会所后面，是一排半开放的打位。球道对面是一片人工湖，湖面上漂着几个白色的浮标，标着距离——五十码、一百码、一百五十码、两百码。顾西辞从球包里抽出一根七号铁杆递给我。

    “握杆给我看看。”

    我接过来，凭着印象摆了个姿势。左手在上右手在下，拇指顺着杆身往下压，膝盖微曲，身体前倾。

    他看了三秒钟，走过来，站在我身后。

    “左手太紧。右手拇指不要压杆身，放在侧面。”

    他的手从后面伸过来，覆在我的手背上，把我的手指一根一根掰到正确的位置。他的手比我大很多，骨节分明，掌心干燥而温热。这个姿势从后面看起来，几乎像是他把我圈在怀里。

    “放松。”他的声音在我耳边响起，气息扫过我的耳廓，“握杆不能太紧。太紧了手腕动不了，挥杆的时候力量传不出去。”

    我深吸一口气，放松手指。他的手从我的手背上移开，退后一步。

    “试试。”

    我挥了一杆。

    球飞出去，划了一道难看的弧线，落在五十码的浮标前面，溅起一小朵水花。

    “重心太靠后了。转移重心的时机不对。”他走过来纠正我的站姿，一只手按在我腰上，把我往前推了一点，“上杆的时候重心移到右脚，下杆的时候重心跟着杆头走，顺势移到左脚。不是用胳膊打球，是用身体转动的力量。你再试一次。”

    他又退开了。

    我在心里数着——左脚重心、右脚重心、转肩、挥杆。

    这一杆打得比刚才好一些，球飞了一百码出头，方向正了很多。

    “有进步。继续。今天先练七号铁杆，打够一百个球再进场地。”

    “一百个？”

    “嫌少？”

    “我以为你会让我打两百个。”

    他坐回遮阳伞下的藤椅上，翘起腿，拿出手机：“看来我确实太仁慈了。”

    我没有再说话，一颗一颗地往球道上打。打到第三十颗的时候手开始酸，第五十颗的时候掌心发红，第七十颗的时候肩膀已经不太听使唤了。但我没有停下来。遮阳伞下那个人看似在看手机，实际上每一次我挥杆的时候，他的余光都扫过来。如果我停下来揉手，他一定会说点什么。不是关心，是那种不咸不淡的评价——累了？合同上可没写体力劳动豁免条款。

    所以我咬着牙继续打。

    打到第九十八颗的时候，身后传来一阵脚步声。一个穿白色衫的中年男人走过来，手里端着一杯威士忌，冰块在杯壁上碰出清脆的声响。

    “顾总，怎么一个人在这儿躲着？”

    许向平。

    我认出了他的脸。万盛集团的执行副总裁，顾西辞昨晚发了一份他的资料给我。四十三岁，清华毕业，娶了林子明的独生女，在万盛干了十五年，从基层做到了二把手。圈内评价是“笑面虎”——脸上永远挂着笑，下手永远不留情。

    “不是一个人。”顾西辞朝我的方向抬了抬下巴，“带了人。”

    许向平的目光移到我身上，上下扫了一遍，嘴角的笑意加深了。

    “这位就是温小姐吧？热搜上见过的。”他走过来，语气热络得像是多年不见的老朋友，“顾总好福气，合同伙伴都这么出众。”

    “许总过奖了。”

    “不是过奖。能在那种场合面不改色地做个PPT提案，这心理素质不是一般人有的。”他转头看顾西辞，“西辞，你这哪是找合约伙伴，分明是挖了个人才。”

    顾西辞放下手机，表情淡淡：“你那边准备好了？陈鹤东呢？”
content_en:
Chapter 3 Swing and Pass
At two o'clock on Saturday afternoon, Gu Xici's car appeared downstairs at the apartment on time.
When I opened the rear door, he was looking down at his phone and said without raising his head: "Sit in front."
“The back seat is roomy.”
"Sit in front. I'm not your driver."
I closed the rear door and got in the passenger seat. There was a faint cedar smell in his car, the scent of car aromatherapy, the same smell as in his office. There was a half-drunk cup of Americano on the center console, and an unopened latte next to it.
"For me?"
"Cheer up. You're going to be on your feet for four hours today."
I took off the lid of my latte and took a sip. Warm, not hot. Gu Xici remembered that I don't drink hot coffee - every time he brought me coffee before, he would ask the clerk to make it warm. How long has this habit been maintained? Eight years or nine years? He hasn't forgotten yet.
"The course is over in Qingcheng. It takes an hour and a half to drive. I'll take this time to tell you the rules." He started the car and turned the steering wheel with one hand. "Today is not a formal game, it is my private practice round. But some of the people present will be participants in next week's invitational tournament. You have to be familiar with their routes in advance."
"Which people?"
"You have met Lin Ziming, from Lin Real Estate. There are three other people today - Xu Xiangping, executive vice president of Wansheng Group, Chen Hedong, who is engaged in private equity, and Zhao Qinian, the owner of Qingcheng Golf Club. Zhao Qinian is not important, Xu Xiangping and Chen Hedong are the ones you want to focus on today."
"Xu Xiangping. Wansheng Group. Is he the one who had friction with you before?"
He glanced sideways at me: "How do you know?"
"I checked. There was a line written in your assistant's memorandum - Xu Xiangping bid with Gu in last year's merger and acquisition case until the last day, and finally lost. There were four words written next to it, the person who came was not malicious."
Gu Xici was silent for a few seconds, then laughed softly: "Did you regard my assistant's memo as an intelligence station?"
"Your assistant is your assistant, not mine. I have to do the back adjustment myself."
"Okay, then do you know who Chen Hedong is?"
"The founder of Zhichun Capital specializes in investing in the consumer field. Last year, he invested in a new tea brand, which quadrupled in half a year. He is called the Midas Touch in the industry, but he has a particularly bad temper. He once forced an entrepreneur to sell his house to pay off his debts because of a gambling agreement."
Gu Xici raised an eyebrow: "How long have you been checking?"
"I checked for two hours last night. You guys have too much public information, including press conferences, interviews, and financial reports. You can build a network of relationships by just browsing."
"Then tell me, what is the relationship between these three people?"
"Xu Xiangping and Chen Hedong are college classmates. They both graduated from Tsinghua University in Economics and Management. Zhao Qinian is Xu Xiangping's brother-in-law, so Qingcheng Club is Xu Xiangping's territory. If you take me to play here today, it is equivalent to planting a Gu family flag in Xu Xiangping's home court."
Gu Xici tapped his fingers twice on the steering wheel. This is his habit when thinking, tapping the nearest thing at hand with his index finger, three times at a time, neither fast nor slow.
"You missed a little," he said.
"Which point?"
"Xu Xiangping's wife is also named Lin. Lin from Lin Real Estate."
"So he is Lin Ziming's son-in-law?"
"That's right."
I redrawn the relationship between these people in my mind. Lin Ziming's son-in-law is Xu Xiangping, Xu Xiangping's college classmate is Chen Hedong, and Xu Xiangping's brother-in-law is the owner of the stadium. This group of people is a family plus an old classmate, and they are all the same. In this situation, Gu Xici was like breaking into someone else's backyard single-handedly.
"What do you want me to do when you brought me here today?"
"Be my partner." His tone was very calm, as if he was saying that the weather was nice today. "The most important test of tacit understanding on the golf course is not the competition between opponents, but the cooperation between partners. When I swing, you have to know where to stand. When I talk to people, you have to know when to speak and when to shut up. You did a good job at Lin's dinner yesterday, but that kind of occasion is easy to deal with - just laugh while holding a wine glass. Today is different."
"What's the difference?"
"Today is not just about socializing, it's about competition. People on the field look down on the vase."
He said the word "vase" very softly, but very clearly. I didn't answer the call.
Qingcheng Golf Club is built on the mountainside, and you can see a panoramic view of the entire course from the parking lot to the clubhouse. The lawn was neatly manicured, the greens were spread like green velvet carpets on the hillside, and the white sand in the bunkers was dazzling in the sun. There is the fragrance of grass clippings and a faint smell of gasoline in the air, the smell of a lawn maintenance truck.
The clubhouse is a Chinese-style building with blue bricks and gray tiles, and two ginkgo trees stand at the door. The waiter was wearing a uniform white shirt and beige vest. When he saw Gu Xici, he came up to him with a well-trained smile on his face.
"Mr. Gu, Mr. Zhao is already waiting for you at the stadium. Mr. Xu and Mr. Chen are also here and are resting in the tea room."
"Let's not go to the tea room yet. Open a training ground for me."
"Okay, please come this way."
The driving range is behind the clubhouse and is a row of semi-open playing positions. Opposite the fairway is an artificial lake, with several white buoys floating on the lake, marking distances - fifty yards, one hundred yards, one hundred and fifty yards, two hundred yards. Gu Xici took out a seven-iron from his golf bag and handed it to me.
"Show me your grip on the pole."
I took it and posed based on my impression. With your left hand on top and your right hand on bottom, press your thumb down along the shaft, bend your knees slightly, and lean forward.
He looked at it for three seconds, then came over and stood behind me.
"The left hand is too tight. Don't press your right thumb on the shaft, put it to the side."
His hand reached out from behind, covering the back of my hand, and moved my fingers to the correct position one by one. His hands are much larger than mine, with distinct joints and dry and warm palms. From behind, this posture almost looks like he is holding me in his arms.
"Relax." His voice rang in my ear, and his breath swept across my ear. "Don't hold the club too tightly. If it is too tight, your wrist will not be able to move, and the power will not be transmitted during the swing."
I took a deep breath and relaxed my fingers. He removed his hand from the back of my hand and stepped back.
"Try it."
I took a swing.
The ball flew out, drew an ugly arc, and landed in front of the fifty-yard buoy, making a small splash.
"The center of gravity is too far back. The timing of shifting the center of gravity is wrong." He came over to correct my stance, put a hand on my waist, and pushed me forward a little. "During the backswing, the center of gravity moved to the right foot. During the downswing, the center of gravity followed the club head and moved to the left foot. You don't use your arms to hit the ball, you use the power of body rotation. You try again."
He backed away again.
I'm counting in my head - left foot, right foot, shoulder turn, swing.
This shot was better than before. The ball flew over a hundred yards and went in a much straighter direction.
"There is progress. Continue. Practice the seven-iron today, and hit a hundred balls before entering the court."
"A hundred?"
"Too little?"
"I thought you were going to let me hit two hundred."
He sat back on the wicker chair under the umbrella, crossed his legs, and took out his mobile phone: "It seems that I am indeed too kind."
I said no more and hit the fairway one by one. When I hit the thirtieth bullet, my hands started to feel sore, when I hit the fiftieth bullet, my palms became red, and when I hit the seventieth bullet, my shoulders no longer worked well. But I didn't stop. The man under the umbrella seemed to be looking at his mobile phone, but in fact every time I swung the golf club, his peripheral vision swept over me. If I stopped to rub my hands, he would definitely say something. It's not a concern, it's a comment that's neither salty nor bland - tired? There is no manual labor exemption clause in the contract.
So I gritted my teeth and kept fighting.
When he hit the ninety-eighth bullet, there was a sound of footsteps behind him. A middle-aged man in a white shirt came over, holding a glass of whiskey in his hand, and the ice cubes made a crisp sound on the side of the glass.
"Mr. Gu, why are you hiding here alone?"
Xu Xiangping.
I recognized his face. Gu Xici, the executive vice president of Wansheng Group, sent me a copy of his information last night. At the age of forty-three, he graduated from Tsinghua University and married Lin Ziming’s only daughter. He worked in Wansheng for fifteen years, rising from the grassroots to the second in command. He is known in the circle as a "smiling tiger" - he always has a smile on his face and never shows mercy.
"Not alone." Gu Xici raised his chin in my direction, "I brought someone with me."
Xu Xiangping's eyes moved to me, scanning up and down, and the smile on his lips deepened.
"This is Miss Wen, right? I saw her on the hot search." He came over and his tone was as warm as an old friend he hadn't seen for many years, "Mr. Gu is so lucky that all our contract partners are so outstanding."
"Mr. Xu has given me the award."
"It's not an award. Being able to make a PPT proposal without hesitation in that kind of situation is not something ordinary people have." He turned to look at Gu Xi Ci, "Xi Ci, you are not looking for a contract partner, you are clearly poaching a talent."
Gu Xici put down his phone and said calmly: "Are you ready over there? Where is Chen Hedong?"
title_en: The Game of True and False Canaries Chapter 3
